title: Mutation and gene editing
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for IB Diploma Biology (review status in the bank: ai-specialist-reviewed-gate-verified-2026-09-21-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms: D1.3#c04, D1.3#c03, D1.3#c10, D1.3#c05. Clues: D1.3#c04 first sentence of the bank's definition; D1.3#c03 first sentence of the bank's definition; D1.3#c10 first sentence of the bank's definition; D1.3#c05 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: D1.3#q01, D1.3#q02, D1.3#q04, D1.3#q07, D1.3#q09, D1.3#q11, D1.3#q13, D1.3#q03, D1.3#q06, D1.3#q08, D1.3#q12, D1.3#q15, D1.3#q17, D1.3#q16, D1.3#q18.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Deletion
items.clue: A gene mutation in which one or more bases are removed from the base sequence of a gene, making the gene shorter.

items.label: Insertion
items.clue: A gene mutation in which one or more extra bases are added to the base sequence of a gene, making the gene longer.

items.label: Mutagen
items.clue: A chemical or physical agent that increases the frequency of gene mutation by damaging DNA or by interfering with DNA replication.

items.label: Single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)
items.clue: A position in the genome at which different individuals in a population carry different bases as a result of a base substitution mutation that has spread in the population.

questions.stem: Part of the base sequence of a gene is GAT TCA GGC ATT before a mutation and GAT TCG GCA TT after it. Which type of gene mutation has occurred?

options.text: A deletion of one base, which has moved every later base one position along
A substitution of the base A by G at the sixth position in the sequence
A chromosome mutation, because the total amount of DNA has changed
A substitution that has shifted the reading frame of later codons

questions.explanation: Aligning the two sequences shows that the A in the second codon is missing and every base after it has moved up one place; the mutant is one base shorter. This is a deletion.

questions.stem: In mRNA the codons GCU, GCC, GCA and GCG all code for alanine. A base substitution in a gene changes the codon GCU in its mRNA to GCC. What is the effect on the polypeptide?

options.text: Alanine is replaced by a different amino acid at that one position
None: the same amino acid, alanine, is placed at that position
The reading frame shifts, changing all amino acids after it
Every amino acid in the polypeptide is changed to another one

questions.stem: One base is deleted from the fourth codon of a gene coding for a polypeptide of 300 amino acids. What is the most likely consequence?

options.text: Only the fourth amino acid is altered, so the polypeptide still works normally
Every one of the 300 amino acids is changed, including the first three
The change is a chromosome mutation, so the gene is not transcribed at all
Almost all of the polypeptide is altered and it ceases to function

questions.stem: Which statement about the causes of gene mutation is correct?

options.text: Gene mutations arise only in cells that are exposed to a mutagen
Microwaves and radio waves are mutagenic just like X-rays
Replication errors can cause mutation without a mutagen
Proofreading by DNA polymerase corrects every error

questions.explanation: Gene mutation is caused by mutagens and by errors in DNA replication or repair. DNA polymerase occasionally pairs a base wrongly, and a small fraction of these errors escape proofreading and repair and become permanent mutations.

questions.stem: Which statement about randomness in mutation is correct?

options.text: Mutations can occur anywhere in the genome, but some bases have a higher probability of mutating than others
Mutations can occur anywhere in the genome, and every base has an identical probability of mutating
Mutations occur in the genes an organism needs to change when its environment changes
Mutations occur only at those bases in the genome that a mutagen has chemically damaged

questions.stem: Which statement about mutations in germ cells and somatic cells is correct?

options.text: A mutation in a skin cell can be inherited by the person's children
Every mutation in a somatic cell causes that cell to become cancerous
A mutation in a germ cell can be passed on to the offspring
A mutation in one liver cell spreads to every body cell

questions.explanation: Germ cells give rise to gametes, so a mutated gene in a germ cell can be passed to the next generation, where it will be present in every cell of the offspring. This is how mutation adds inherited variation to a species.

questions.stem: Why is gene mutation described as the original source of all genetic variation?

options.text: New alleles arise only by mutation; meiosis and fertilization just recombine alleles that already exist
Crossing over in meiosis creates new alleles, and mutation adds to the variation they produce
Most mutations are beneficial, so each one adds a useful new variant to the species
Organisms generate new alleles whenever their environment demands a new trait from them

questions.stem: The same gene was sequenced in 1000 people. At one position 62% carry C and 38% carry T, and the two resulting codons code for the same amino acid. How should this difference be described?

options.text: A rare mutation causing disease in the 38% group
A frameshift mutation that affects later codons
An SNP that leaves the polypeptide unchanged
A substitution that changes one amino acid

questions.explanation: A single base differs between individuals at one position: this is a single-nucleotide polymorphism, the result of a base substitution that has spread in the population. Because both codons specify the same amino acid, the polypeptide is unchanged.

questions.stem: Why is a polypeptide likely to cease functioning when several hundred bases are deleted from the middle of its gene?

options.text: Only because a deletion of any size shifts the reading frame of every later codon
So many amino acids are missing that the polypeptide cannot fold into its working shape
Only the amino acids coded by the deleted bases are missing; the rest still folds as normal
The amino acids coded before the deletion are also changed by the loss of bases

questions.stem: Cultures of cells were exposed separately to (i) ultraviolet light, (ii) visible light and (iii) nitrous acid, a chemical that alters bases in DNA. Which treatments are expected to raise the mutation rate above the background rate?

options.text: (i), (ii) and (iii), because light and chemicals both damage DNA
(iii) only, because radiation from non-radioactive sources is harmless
None of them, because DNA repair enzymes correct all of the damage
(i) and (iii), because both chemically alter the bases in DNA

questions.stem: A mutation occurs in a gene that controls the cell cycle in one cell lining a man's colon. Which statement about the consequences is correct?

options.text: The mutation will be passed on to all of the man's children
The mutation will spread to every cell in the man's body
The cell has become cancerous, as does every mutated somatic cell
The cell may divide uncontrollably and form a tumour

questions.explanation: Genes controlling the cell cycle keep cell division under control. A mutation in such a gene in a somatic cell can allow the cell and its descendants to divide without restraint, which is how cancer begins; several such mutations are usually needed before a tumour forms.

questions.stem: Researchers want to investigate the function of gene Z in mice. They obtain a strain from a knockout library in which gene Z is inoperative. How should they use it?

options.text: Conclude that Z has no function if the knockout mice appear normal
Check first that the whole of gene Z has been cut out of the chromosome
Compare the phenotype of the knockout mice with that of normal mice
Block the protein made by gene Z in adult mice and observe the effect

questions.stem: In CRISPR–Cas9 gene editing, what determines the position in the genome at which the DNA is cut?

options.text: The base sequence of the guide RNA, which pairs with the complementary sequence in the target DNA
The active site of the Cas9 enzyme, which recognises the target DNA base sequence directly
The guide RNA, which cuts both strands of the DNA at the position where it binds to it
The sequence of the new bases that Cas9 itself inserts into the gene to rewrite it

questions.stem: Mice in which gene P has been knocked out show no detectable difference from normal mice under standard laboratory conditions. What is the best conclusion?

options.text: P has no function, because removing its product produced no change in the mice's phenotype
The knockout did not work, because the sequence of P is still present in the genome
The protein made by P is still active because only the gene, not the protein, was altered
P may have a function masked by another gene or shown only in untested conditions

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the successful use of CRISPR–Cas9 gene editing?

options.text: Editing the skin cells of adults with sickle cell disease so that all their own children inherit the corrected gene
Editing the blood-forming stem cells of patients with sickle cell disease so that they produce fetal haemoglobin
Using Cas9 itself both to cut out the faulty bases and to write the corrected sequence into the gene
Using guide RNA on its own to cut out the faulty base from the gene in a patient's blood cells
